title: evidence_refs entry (evidence-format-neutral)
description: A single entry in an implementation conformance result row's evidence_refs array. This slot is intentionally evidence-format neutral: a Settlement Attestation Receipt (SAR) is ONE type that can fill it, not the only one. Any other verifiable evidence format (a signed log entry, a different receipt scheme, a hash-chained ledger export, etc.) can occupy the same slot using its own `type` value.

type.description: Evidence format identifier. 'sar' is one recognized value; implementations are free to define others (e.g. 'ledger_entry', 'signed_log', 'custom').

uri.description: Location where the evidence can be independently fetched or resolved.

digest.description: Content digest of the evidence artifact, for tamper-evidence. Algorithm prefix required.

receipt_profile.description: Optional. Only meaningful when type == 'sar'. Names the receipt profile, e.g. 'sar-402' for the x402-adjacent SAR profile. Absent or ignored for non-SAR evidence types.

verification_hint.description: Optional. A short human-readable pointer to how a third party can independently verify this evidence (e.g. a CLI command, an API endpoint, a spec URL). Not itself proof of anything.

boundary.description: What this evidence attests to and, just as importantly, what it does NOT attest to. Required so evidence_refs entries cannot be read as broader claims than they support (e.g. a SAR attests to a delivery/verification boundary event, not payment finality or legal finality).
examples: delivery-boundary evidence only; not proof of payment or legal finality

demonstration.description: Optional. If true, this evidence_ref points to a demo/example artifact rather than evidence tied to a specific production transaction. MUST be set true when referencing demo receipts (e.g. defaultverifier.com/demo/sar-402).
